newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul confirms bank ownership limit will not change.
newsitem.headline: Seoul confirms bank ownership limit will not change.

text.p: South Korea's finance ministry officially announced on Tuesday that it had decided to keep the individual ownership ceiling in commercial banks at the current four percent.
"The government has decided to maintain the ceiling on ownership in bank shares at the current four percent for the time being," a ministry statement said.
The announcement was in line with remarks earlier on Tuesday by a senior ministry official, who told Reuters by telephone the current ceiling would be retained.

The decision was in contrast to an earlier proposal by the Presidential Commission for Financial Reform to expand the limit to 10 percent under certain conditions to enhance the competitiveness of the local banking industry.

However, the statement said the ministry would accept another proposal by the commission that the top five industrial conglomerates be allowed to have non-permanent directors on the board of directors of banks in which they are major shareholders.
The statement said institutional investors, excluding banks, would also be allowed to sit on the board of directors.

It said the ministry would allow establishment of a financial holding company which can set up wholly owned banks or non-bank financial firms. But the individual ownership in a bank's holding company would be limited at four percent.
